property_summary: For every interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true if and only if interfaceId matches type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId; the bug returns true for all interfaceIds, violating this rule for random interfaceIds.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return the same boolean as (interfaceId == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId || interfaceId == type(IERC165).interfaceId); the bug returns true for all interfaceIds, violating this for any other value.
For any interfaceId, supportsInterface must return the same as the reference implementation's logic; the mutant returns true for all IDs, violating this for IDs not matching the two known interfaces.
C.supportsInterface must return true for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId and type(IERC165).interfaceId per the OZ pattern, but the mutant returns false for all inputs.
For any interfaceId that is type(IAccessControl).interfaceId or type(IERC165).interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true, but the mutant returns false for all inputs.
For any input bytes4, the reference C.supportsInterface must return true for type(IERC165).interfaceId, while the mutant returns false, violating ERC-165 compliance.

For any interfaceId, C.supportsInterface must return the result of the canonical ERC165 check: (interfaceId == type(IERC165).interfaceId) || (interfaceId == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId); the mutant returns false for all inputs.
The reference contract returns true when supportsInterface is called with type(IERC165).interfaceId, the mutant returns false, breaking ERC-165 conformance.
supportsInterface must return true for ERC165 interface ID because C inherits ERC165, but the bug removes this check so it returns false.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for type(IERC165).interfaceId in the correct contract because it inherits ERC165, but the buggy contract where the super call is removed returns false for that ID.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for type(IERC165).interfaceId AND must return true for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId if and only if that interfaceId equals type(IAccessControl).interfaceId; the buggy version returns false for type(IERC165).interfaceId, breaks the ERC165 contract.
supportsInterface must return true for type(IERC165).interfaceId because C inherits ERC165, but the buggy version skips the ERC165 check and returns false for it.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for type(IERC165).interfaceId in the correct contract because it inherits ERC165, but the buggy version where the super call is removed returns false for that ID.
For any role that has been granted to an account, hasRole must return true; the mutant returns false for all roles and accounts, breaking this invariant for any granted role.

For any input, if hasRole returns false in both the reference and the mutant, that is consistent; but if the reference returns true, the mutant must also return true due to identical role state, yet the mutant always returns false, so the invariant 'hasRole returns the same boolean for any admissible input' is broken by the mutant for any role that was granted.

When the DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE (0x00) is initially granted to the contract itself in the constructor, `hasRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, address(c))` should return true in the reference contract, but the mutant always returns false.
For any role and account, `hasRole` must return true if and only if the role was granted to that account; the mutant always returns false, so after granting a role, `hasRole` differs.
For any role and account, hasRole must return true if and only if the role has been granted to that account; the mutant always returns false, violating this for any granted role.

For any role and account, hasRole must return true only when the account was granted that role (via grantRole or _setupRole); the mutant returns true for random roles and accounts that were never granted the role.

For any role, getRoleAdmin must return the stored admin role, not a constant zero; the mutant returns bytes32(0) instead of the actual admin role, breaking the rule for any role whose admin was set to a non-zero value.

For any role, getRoleAdmin must return the stored admin role; the mutant returns bytes32(0) regardless of the actual stored admin role, so setting a role's admin to a non-zero value and reading it back will differ.
For any role whose admin has been set to a non-zero value, getRoleAdmin must return that admin; the mutant returns bytes32(0) breaking the rule.
For any role whose admin is set to a non-zero value via _setRoleAdmin, getRoleAdmin must return that non-zero admin; the mutant returns bytes32(0) instead of the stored admin, violating the rule.
For any role whose admin role has been changed to a non-zero value, getRoleAdmin must return that non-zero value; the mutant returns bytes32(0) instead.
